Rebuild an analysis and compare its files with a completed build

Source: R/reproduce.R
projr_reproduce.Rd

Clone a trusted analysis, restore its recorded inputs and run its production scripts from empty output folders. projr compares the resulting files with the build's recorded filenames and hashes. The scripts and hooks run with your usual R permissions. The replay itself creates no version or release.

Usage

projr_reproduce(
  repo,
  branch = NULL,
  version = NULL,
  commit = NULL,
  path = tempfile("projr-reproduce-"),
  destination = "archive"
)

Arguments

repo

A GitHub repository in owner/repo form, optionally followed by @branch, or a local Git repository.

branch

Branch to search. Defaults to the repository's default branch.

version

Exact completed build version, with or without a leading v.

commit

Full or abbreviated commit SHA on the selected branch. Alone, it selects the last completed build at or before this commit and runs that build's code. With version, it selects the code to run against that version's inputs and expected outputs.

path

New or empty directory for the clone. By default it is created in the R session's temporary directory. Supply a path to keep the results.

destination

GitHub archive title or release tag for recovering missing snapshots and inputs. Defaults to "archive".

Value

A list with exact for the whole comparison, a directories data frame with one row per output or documentation directory and counts of identical, changed, missing and extra files, and a files data frame with each label, relative path and status. The result also identifies the checkout path, version, code commit, build record commit and dependency method. dependencies$packages lists package names and versions and dependencies$pinned indicates whether the run used a lockfile. A missing baseline cannot produce an exact match.

Details

With neither selector, reproduce the latest completed build on the branch. A version on its own selects that build and its code. With a lockfile, projr restores its package versions with renv. With only a DESCRIPTION, pak installs its dependencies and their versions are unpinned. With neither file, the analysis uses the available R libraries. The input, output and cache paths used during replay must be inside the clone. Archives can be stored elsewhere.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
result <- projr_reproduce("owner/study", branch = "analysis", version = "1.2.3")
result$exact
subset(result$files, status != "identical")
} # }
